title: Petra and the Playlist
premise: Coral Sandoval, a seventeen-year-old debate champion, has spent ten years carefully managing her family's silence around the disappearance of her uncle Mateo — until she finds coded directions hidden in her grandmother's recipe box that lead not to food but to evidence of who framed him. Following the playlist-coded clues, Coral and her best friend Priya uncover that the town's beloved judge built his career on Mateo's conviction. As the final audition for nationals collides with the deadline to expose the truth, Coral must choose between the careful lie her family has lived and a public truth that could cost her Priya's trust — because Priya's father is the judge's protégé. In the end, Coral tells the whole story on stage at auditions, winning neither the trophy nor back Priya immediately, but freeing her family and earning a fragile, honest beginning.
about_author: Coral Fairweather is a former high-school debate coach from coastal Oregon who writes stories about kids who are braver in real life than on scorecards. She collects recipe boxes at estate sales and swears half of them hold secrets.

chapters.title: The Careful Girl
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. At a debate tournament she dismantles an opponent effortlessly, then comes home to a dinner where her mother deflects every question about Uncle Mateo's tenth missing-persons anniversary. The beat: competence in public, suffocation at home.

chapters.title: Cardamom and Ciphers
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Cleaning out grandma Rosa's kitchen, Coral finds a recipe card titled 'Mateo's Favorite' whose instructions make no culinary sense — measurements spell letters, temperatures mark dates. Emotional beat: the first crack in ten years of carefulness.

chapters.title: Side B
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The cards reference songs; Coral realizes they map to a mixtape buried in the garage. She decodes the first track title into a location: the old record shop. Beat: thrill curdling into fear as she understands this was deliberate.

chapters.title: Priya Knows Everything Except This
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya notices Coral lying badly for the first time in their friendship and feels the sting of exclusion. Meanwhile her father, Judge Herrera's protégé, praises 'the Sandoval tragedy' at dinner. Beat: loyalty tested by secrecy.

chapters.title: Static on Kettle Street
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. At the shuttered record shop, Coral finds a locker keyed to the second song. Inside: a cassette, a photograph of Mateo with Judge Herrera the week before he vanished, and a note in Rosa's handwriting: 'He saw what the judge did.' Beat: vertigo.

chapters.title: What Grandma Buried
chapters.summary: Rosa's POV, 1998 flashback. Rosa watches Mateo come home shaken after finding ledgers in Herrera's chambers, then helps him hide copies inside his mixtapes. Beat: a mother choosing protection over truth, planting the seed of everything.

chapters.title: The Argument She Can't Win
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral confronts her mother with the photo; her mother forbids her to dig, revealing the family once tried and got threatened. Beat: Coral understands the carefulness was armor — and refuses it anyway.

chapters.title: Track Three
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The third song leads to the marina and a witness: Dee, the shop owner's sister, who confirms Mateo came to her the night he disappeared carrying a tape. Beat: hope with teeth.

chapters.title: Audition Season
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Nationals audition prep begins; Coral is distracted and off-beat in their duo piece. Priya demands honesty, gets a partial truth, and accepts it — for now. Beat: friendship stretched, not snapped.

chapters.title: The Judge's Kindness
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Judge Herrera, charming and paternal, offers Coral a scholarship letter of recommendation — and mentions, softly, that families that stir up old grief often regret it. Beat: menace wearing a cardigan.

chapters.title: Rewind
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral plays Mateo's cassette: his voice narrating the ledger numbers — payments to Herrera, a covered-up construction death. Someone recorded over part of it. Beat: proof exists, but incomplete.

chapters.title: The Missing Verse
chapters.summary: Dee's POV. Dee admits she kept one tape back as insurance and lost it years ago — or gave it away. Her guilt unspools; she points to the last name on the playlist: a boy who idolized Mateo. Beat: the past demanding payment.

chapters.title: Follow That Song
chapters.summary: Coral and Priya's alternating POV. The trail leads to a storage auction; Priya, now fully inside the secret, uses her father's courthouse access to trace the buyer. Beat: partnership reborn, deeper than before.

chapters.title: What Priya Found Out
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The buyer was Priya's own father, acting for Herrera. She reads the ledger copy herself and must decide whether her family's name matters more than the truth. Beat: betrayal as inheritance.

chapters.title: Interference
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The scholarship offer is quietly withdrawn; her mother's workplace gets inspected; someone follows Coral home. Beat: pressure designed to look like coincidence.

chapters.title: The Fight Before the Final
chapters.summary: Priya and Coral's alternating POV. Priya wants to go to the press; Coral wants airtight proof first so it can't be spun away. Their argument detonates into old wounds about trust. Beat: the friendship breaks on the fault line of method.

chapters.title: Solo
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral preps the audition alone, running her debate skills against her own case and finding the holes. Rosa, frail but sharp, gives her the final card: the location of Mateo's original notebook. Beat: grief converted to strategy.

chapters.title: The Notebook
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. In the courthouse archive, behind the plaque honoring Herrera, Coral retrieves Mateo's notebook — full names, dates, the construction site foreman's confession. A security guard nearly catches her. Beat: terror and triumph in equal measure.

chapters.title: Final Audition
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. On stage before judges including Herrera's circle, Coral abandons her prepared piece and performs the story: the playlist, the ledgers, the notebook, naming names. Beat: the climax — truth as the only winning argument.

chapters.title: Aftermath in D Minor
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The story goes public; Herrera resigns under investigation; Priya's father faces consequences too. Priya, humiliated and grieving, still shows up at Coral's door. Beat: cost acknowledged, forgiveness begun but not finished.

chapters.title: Mateo's Voice
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Police reopen the case; a witness comes forward about the night Mateo disappeared. Coral plays the restored cassette for her mother, and the family finally says his name out loud together. Beat: memory reclaimed from silence.

chapters.title: Encore
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, epilogue. Months later, Coral loses the national final gracefully and doesn't mind; she and Priya start a podcast telling cold cases through music. The last scene: adding a new recipe card to Rosa's box — blank, waiting. Beat: belonging rebuilt on truth.
